purpose: Skeleton-first foot audit. Test the user's observed oversized-foot issue against measurement-compatible adult male metatarsal/phalangeal radiographic data.

measurement_compatibility.metatarsals: Strong. Patil 2017 measures distal metatarsal head to midpoint of base articular surface; a003 uses TMT/base to metatarsal head.
measurement_compatibility.proximal_middle_phalanges: Moderate-to-strong. Patil uses articular-surface midpoint to midpoint; a003 uses joint/station endpoints.
measurement_compatibility.distal_phalanges: Weaker. a003 distal segments terminate at a tip station that may include soft tissue beyond the distal phalanx.

hallux_distal_phalanx.measurement_warning: a003 distal phalanx tail may extend to a surface/toe-tip station; direct osteometric equivalence is weaker than for metatarsals/proximal/middle phalanges.

toe2_distal_phalanx.measurement_warning: a003 distal phalanx tail may extend to a surface/toe-tip station; direct osteometric equivalence is weaker than for metatarsals/proximal/middle phalanges.

findings: The current BODY SURFACE foot-length defect remains confirmed: r95/a003 heel-to-toe skin length is ~305 mm versus a stature-conditioned ANSUR expectation of ~280 mm (z +2.77).

The earlier single-source conclusion that all a003 metatarsals are definitively too long is withdrawn. They are >2 SD above the Patil 2017 male means, but independent stature-regression studies from Spain, Portugal and Korea imply larger M1/M2 values at 1.82 m and use different maximum-length definitions.
Therefore the forefoot skeleton remains REOPEN, but the reason is measurement/source conflict plus the clearly long surface foot—not a proven requirement to shorten every metatarsal by 12–19 mm.
Toe proximal/middle segments also appear long against Patil 2017, but stature/population conditioning and endpoint definitions must be triangulated before exact shortening is selected.
The canonical foot must be built from endpoint-matched hindfoot/midfoot/forefoot evidence and then the mesh shortened around the finished chain.

provisional_target_corridors_mm.note: Patil 2017 ±1 SD bands remain one evidence band only, not canonical target corridors. Stature-conditioned studies conflict materially and must be reconciled by endpoint definition.

next_steps: Map a003 metatarsal control endpoints to each source's maximum/physiological/head-to-base definition.
Use at least two endpoint-compatible stature-aware sources before freezing M1/M2; obtain equivalent evidence for M3-M5.
Triangulate toe phalanx lengths with stature/sex-aware data or multi-population ratios.
Build hindfoot/midfoot contact-centre targets separately, then derive final heel-to-toe skeleton and explicit soft-tissue allowances.
Only after canonical foot geometry is frozen should the production mesh foot be shortened.

stature_conditioned_crosscheck.interpretation: These stature regressions use maximum/osteometric/radiographic metatarsal definitions and different populations. They show that the earlier Patil-mean comparison cannot by itself prove that a003 metatarsals are pathologically long: at 1.82 m, independent equations imply substantially longer M1/M2 values than the Patil sample means and values near or above the a003 spans.

audit_correction_2026_10_08.reason: A single healthy-male radiographic sample was incorrectly treated as sufficient proof that the metatarsal skeleton was too long.
audit_correction_2026_10_08.correction: Added three stature-regression datasets with different populations/measurement definitions. They materially change the interpretation at 1.82 m.
audit_correction_2026_10_08.retained_fact: The r95/a003 surface foot is still clearly long relative to the stature-conditioned ANSUR distribution.
audit_correction_2026_10_08.consequence: Do not shorten every metatarsal to the Patil means. Reconstruct endpoint-matched canonical bone lengths first.
